source: Library of Congress, Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, St. Louis Vol. 12 (1938, revised to 1950), sheet 53, image 04858_12_1950-0053
labeled_by: AI-assisted draft from the 1938 key: each site compared with the 1950 scan side by side, 2026-10-19
scope: Industrial, fuel, tank and vehicle-service uses, plus stores and warehouses for paint, hardware or building materials, plus every G.T. symbol. Excludes dwellings, general stores and flats, offices, clinics, banks, post offices, general/grocery/furniture/merchandise storage, and auto houses (A) with no other use. Groups (a field of tanks) are one entry.

definitions.gasoline_tank_count: Number of G.T. / G.T.S. symbols drawn for this site. 0 means none drawn.
definitions.other_tanks: Tanks that are not G.T. symbols (water, grain, iron, fuel oil, etc.).
definitions.map_notes: Only what is printed on the sheet.
definitions.interpretation: Inference, not a map fact; never scored.

sheet_layout: S Broadway runs down the middle (Quincy at top, Robert at bottom). Pennsylvania Ave is the left edge; the M.P. R.R. tracks and an unopened Water St are on the right.

buildings.label: BAUR FLOUR MILLS CO.
buildings.construction: brick (shipping room frame; grain tanks concrete; head house iron-clad)
buildings.map_notes: Flour mill, capacity 50 bbl per 24 hrs. Office (2½), warehouse (2), mill (5), motor room, flour warehouse, frame shipping room. Elevator 6,000 bu, crib construction. 6 grain tanks 54 ft high, capacity 85,000 bu, fireproof (concrete), with a 2-story iron-clad head house 28 ft high on the tanks. Watchman, no clock. Heat: steam. Power: electric. Chemical extinguishers, barrels & pails.
